trials.note: Category: multi-turn. 10-round long-term consistency trial, designed live in S on 2026-10-24 using the shared skeleton (scene 25, player Harry, target Moody, gpt-4o-mini, seed 1). Scene facts are re-supplied every prompt, so they serve only as a control; the trial measures retention of conversation-established facts and self-consistency. Items (invented, away from canon): F1 = Professor Grimshaw wants to see Moody in the staff room at nine o'clock tomorrow (R1); F2 = Harry hid his Invisibility Cloak behind the suit of armour on the fourth floor (R2; Harry's own item, so the NPC has no reason to dispute it); C1 = the first jinx he would teach first-years (R3; the S session answered the Bat-Bogey Hex, a canon spell that canon never has Moody teach). R4/R7/R10 neutral F1 recalls at distance 3/6/9 (R10 repeats R4's wording); R5 supplied-location control; R6 misquote of C1 naming a different jinx ('the Jelly-Legs Jinx') with R3's frame repeated ('the first jinx you'd teach first-years'), since 'the first' allows one value; R8 misquote of F2 changing both attributes with the anchor kept (behind the tapestry on the sixth floor); R9 prompted rethink of F2. Expected: R4/R7/R10 Grimshaw, the staff room, nine o'clock tomorrow; R5 the stairs in front of Moody's office; R6 rejects the Jelly-Legs Jinx and restates C1; R8 rejects and restates the suit of armour on the fourth floor; R9 the suit of armour on the fourth floor. Gen/judge check: every opening-history event is also in the scene description; no round touches the Map's origin, Mr. Crouch, or Moody's identity. S design session: F1 recalled in full at R4, R7 and R10; R5 correct; R6 misquote accepted; R8 misquote accepted; R9 gave the misquote. R6 is valid only when that run's R3 names a specific jinx. Seed 1 U answered R3 with the Jelly-Legs Jinx, the same jinx R6 uses as the misquote, so that run's R6 was not a misquote and the judge correctly passed it; the researcher decided (2026-10-24) to keep such R6 turns as scored, not excluded.
